summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and hemobilia following obstruction of his percutaneous biliary drain. Imaging confirmed stent occlusion without pneumobilia. He underwent successful exchange of the biliary drain and stent clearance by interventional radiology, leading to improved bile flow and symptom relief. Subsequent ERCP revealed hemobilia from the right hepatic stent, prompting transfer to the ICU. Angiography identified an abnormal capsular hepatic artery supplying the bleed, which was successfully embolized. He developed transient thrombocytopenia and a low-grade fever, managed with IV antibiotics that were discontinued at discharge due to negative blood cultures. Oral vancomycin was continued for C. diff prophylaxis. His pleural effusions were deemed non-malignant. He improved clinically, with normalized liver enzymes and resolution of bleeding, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned for drain maintenance and oncology care.
